profile.address: Lookout Drive, Garland, Dallas County, Texas, 75044
profile.reading: This point is one of four building footprints OpenStreetMap contributors have mapped as NTT in a roughly 600-meter cluster just south of Lookout Drive in Garland, TX, the same street NTT's own site gives for its confirmed Dallas TX1 (2008 Lookout Dr, 230,000 square feet, 16 megawatts of critical IT load, with SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, NIST 800-53 High, and HIPAA attestations) and Dallas TX4 (2060 Lookout Dr, 127,000 square feet, 36 megawatts, part of a 124-megawatt planned campus, available from June 2026) buildings; data center directory Baxtel additionally lists TX2 at 2108 Lookout Dr and TX3 at 2080 Lookout Dr. An earlier reverse-geocoding pass on this point's own coordinates returned a nearby but unrelated street name (North President George Bush Highway), which this entry does not repeat as a confirmed address; a direct comparison of this way's own node coordinates against NTT's documented Lookout Drive buildings instead places it within the same tight campus cluster as the other three mapped NTT buildings in this immediate area. Because this way lacks an address or building-reference tag of its own, this entry cannot confirm which specific NTT building (TX1, TX2, TX3, or TX4) it corresponds to, and does not guess; it is presented as part of the shared Garland, TX data center campus rather than assigned a false building-specific address or capacity figure. RagingWire (NTT's US brand) announced this campus in 2022 as a planned 1-million-square-foot, 80-megawatt-plus development, since expanded further per the individual building figures above. Data Center Frontier toured TX1 and reports the Garland campus was established in 2016 on the former RagingWire site and has been operational since 2017, with the 42-acre megacampus ultimately planned to hold over one million square feet and 144 megawatts of critical IT load at full buildout. NTT announced a 50 million dollar fit out of the TX2 and TX3 buildings in June 2023, adding nearly 300,000 square feet of data vault and office space with each building rated at 36 megawatts, using air cooled chillers with fan coil wall designs distinct from TX1s original cooling configuration. A further 42 million dollar, 236,000 square foot fourth building was reported under construction from September 2025 through an expected April 2026 completion, expanding the 47 acre site. Cushman and Wakefield market data cited alongside that expansion put existing Dallas-Fort Worth data center capacity at 4.5 million square feet by the end of 2023 with only 178,000 square feet available for lease, reflecting the tight vacancy driving continued campus growth at this site.

reading.body:
NTT's Garland campus sits on a 47-acre cluster of four buildings on Lookout Drive in Dallas County, with two buildings publishing their specifications: TX1 at 16 megawatts of critical IT load across 230,000 square feet, and TX4 at 36 megawatts across 127,000 square feet, for a confirmed 52 megawatts among published buildings. NTT has announced a planned campus total of 144 megawatts at full buildout across over one million square feet, though capacity is not published for the two intermediate buildings TX2 and TX3. At an assumption of 40 kilowatts per rack, a common AI training density, the 52 published megawatts represent roughly 1,300 racks in the two named buildings alone. The campus opened in 2017 on the former RagingWire site and has expanded continuously since, with TX2 and TX3 completed in 2023 after a 50 million dollar fitout and TX4 scheduled for June 2026 completion after a 42 million dollar expansion from April 2026.

The campus qualifies to host compliance-sensitive workloads: TX1 holds SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, NIST 800-53 High, and HIPAA attestations. The two buildings use distinct cooling architectures, with TX1 relying on earlier configuration and TX2 and TX3 using air-cooled chillers with fan coil wall designs. Neither the operator nor sources cite GPU density, power-draw specifications per rack, or current tenant usage.

Texas published 468 megawatts of data center capacity across 133 mapped facilities as of this reading, with only 18 facilities publishing megawatt figures. This campus's confirmed 52 megawatts does not rank it in the top 18 by published capacity statewide, placing it outside the state's measurable tier. At the Dallas-Fort Worth regional level, capacity stood at 4.5 million square feet by end of 2023 with only 178,000 square feet available for lease, a 4 percent vacancy rate that has driven the continued expansion announced at this site.
